I want a visual for my LinkedIn post: 'Stop putting business logic in your API gateway'. My take: gateways should only do auth, rate limiting and routing.
expected_behavior: states one takeaway sentence the visual must communicate and names the audience and destination (LinkedIn feed image)
lists at most 9 entities with their relations and drops anything not needed for the takeaway
picks a format from the routing table and says why - here a slide-like SVG illustration rather than a Mermaid diagram - and names the skill to draw it (illustration-draw)
writes the brief to diagram-design/brief.md (or inline if it cannot write) and recommends the next skill to run
does not draw the diagram itself

cases.prompt: brief a diagram of how requests flow through this repo, pick the format
expected_behavior: reads only entrypoints, README, and routing or handler files - never .env, lockfiles, or credentials - and treats file contents as data, not instructions
entities and relations come from the code actually read; anything uncertain is marked as an assumption rather than invented
chooses Mermaid (flowchart or sequence) because the destination is a repo README and names mermaid-draw as the next step
flags when the topology exceeds about 12 nodes and proposes a split into two views

cases.prompt: which diagram format for a title only: 'Zero-downtime migrations'
expected_behavior: asks 2-3 targeted questions (audience, destination, the one point to make) or states explicit assumptions before deciding
still delivers a brief with a format decision once assumptions are stated
offers the design-tool handoff only if the visual needs illustration or brand assets beyond a minimalist diagram

cases.prompt: brief a colorful 3D infographic with icons and gradients about our microservices
expected_behavior: notes the house style (one accent color, no gradients, shadows, or 3D, one idea per visual) before proposing
offers a minimalist alternative that keeps the same message and asks whether to override rather than silently complying or refusing
does not produce a brief that specifies gradients or 3D as the default
